analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [Project Gutenberg's official catalog documentation](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html)
identifies machine-readable catalogs, OPDS and affiliate/mirror links. Use the
catalog as a retrieval model; mirrors are duplicate hosting. National libraries,
state digital libraries, regional literary organizations and university special
collections supply additional independent origins. The [Library of Congress
JSON/YAML interface](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) is a US starting
point for digitized collection records; its scope is not the entire library catalog.
DPLA's [developer documentation](https://pro.dp.la/developers/api-codex) is a
US aggregator lead requiring a fresh documentation/access check before selection.

analysis_refs.heading: C17 — Newspapers, magazines and public-interest articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Separate historic newspaper repositories from current
publishers. The [Library of Congress Chronicling America API page](https://www.loc.gov/apis/additional-apis/chronicling-america-api/)
states that the collection moved exclusively to the loc.gov API beginning in
2025; do not reuse old `chroniclingamerica.loc.gov` integration recipes.
Europeana and national libraries provide additional historical leads. For current
US/local journalism, [INN's Find Your News directory](https://findyournews.org/)
leads to publishers by place and topic. India's
[Press Registrar title directory](https://prgi.gov.in/en/test/registred-titles)
supports discovery by publication place, state and language. Registration proves
neither free article access nor permission to reuse metadata.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Ten new integrations are released behind `CONTENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED=true`:
Global Digital Library, LibriVox, Library of Congress digital books, Biodiversity
Heritage Library's Internet Archive collection, African Minds, LSE Press,
Mattering Press, mediastudies.press, punctum books and Python 3.15 documentation.
Five publisher catalogs share Thoth; this is not five separate API infrastructures.
The existing Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and StoryWeaver snapshots
and the existing OpenAlex/Europe PMC integrations are also selectable. With the
existing production flags, this gives 16 connected sources, not 16 fully audited
origins or complete catalogs.
